summary: Describes Oblivious DNS over HTTPS, a protocol where a proxy relays encrypted DoH messages so a client's IP address is hidden from the DNS resolver. No single server sees both who asked and what was asked. It was developed outside the IETF and published for interoperability and experimentation. It is experimental.

eli5.summary: A messenger carries a sealed question, so the answerer never knows who sent it.

questions: how to hide ip from dns resolver
subtitle: Hide DNS queries from resolvers using a privacy-preserving relay.

tldr.problem: Standard DNS and even DNS over HTTPS (DoH) require the client to reveal its IP address to the DNS resolver, allowing the resolver to link queries to users.
tldr.mechanism: Oblivious DoH introduces a proxy that relays encrypted DNS messages, ensuring no single server knows both who queried and what was queried.
tldr.outcome: Clients can query DNS without revealing their identity to resolvers, but the protocol is experimental and requires coordinating between independent proxy and resolver services.

today: RFC 9230 is an experimental specification published in June 2022. It is not an Internet Standard and is under evaluation for real-world deployment impacts and performance. The protocol remains experimental pending broader adoption and standardization efforts.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Clients using DNS over HTTPS (DoH) gain privacy from eavesdroppers, but they must still reveal their IP address to the resolver. This leak allows the resolver to correlate queries with users. Oblivious DoH solves this by inserting a proxy between the client and the resolver, ensuring no single entity knows both the client IP and the query contents.

The protocol uses encryption to guarantee that the proxy sees only network metadata, the resolver sees only encrypted queries, and only the client holds the decryption keys.
sections.eli5: Your question goes in a sealed box that only the answerer can open. The mail carrier sees the box is moving but not what is inside or who it is for.

sections.title: The Three-Party Architecture
sections.content:
Oblivious DoH involves three entities: the Client sends encrypted queries through an Oblivious Proxy to an Oblivious Target. The client encrypts queries using the target's public key, so only the target can decrypt them. The proxy forwards the encrypted blob and returns the encrypted response without ever seeing the plaintext query.

The target resolves the query and encrypts the response using keying material derived during the query decryption process. The client then uses the same keying material to decrypt the answer. This split of knowledge ensures that if an attacker compromises either the proxy or the target (but not both), the attacker still learns nothing about the relationship between client IP and query contents.
sections.eli5: You write your question, seal it with the answerer's lock, and give it to a helper. The helper carries it without knowing what is inside. Only the answerer can open it and write a reply sealed for you alone.

sections.title: Protocol Encoding
sections.content:
Oblivious DoH messages carry a message type (query or response), a key ID to identify which public key was used, and the encrypted message itself. Queries use message type 0x01 and responses use 0x02. The key ID allows the target to look up the correct decryption key without learning which client sent the query.

Messages include the full DNS request or response plus optional padding (zeros) to obscure message lengths from traffic analysis. The protocol uses HPKE (Hybrid Public Key Encryption) with a base cipher suite of DHKEM(X25519), HKDF-SHA256, and AES-128-GCM, though applications can define other suites.
sections.eli5: The message is labeled with which lock was used, but not with who sent it. Extra padding is added so eavesdroppers cannot guess what the message says from its size.

sections.title: Security and Privacy
sections.content:
The protocol assumes the client trusts that the proxy and target do not collude. An attacker who compromises both parties can link queries to client IPs. The specification models this as an extended Dolev-Yao attacker that can observe all network traffic and compromise either the proxy or the target but not the client.

Traffic analysis remains possible; observers can count query frequency and sizes. The specification recommends padding guidance from RFC 8467 to mitigate this. Additionally, proxies can throttle clients based on decryption errors, and targets can rate-limit requests. Targets should not identify clients via authentication mechanisms that proxies could leak to proxies.
sections.eli5: If the helper and answerer work together against you, they can figure out you sent the question. Both are trusted separately but not together.

sections.title: Deployment and Experimentation
sections.content:
Oblivious DoH is an experimental protocol developed outside the IETF to enable real-world deployment and evaluation. The experiment aims to measure performance impacts, particularly latency and DNS resolution times. Participants will test different discovery and configuration mechanisms for proxies and targets, including connection reuse and pooling.

The protocol specifies a media type, application/oblivious-dns-message, for HTTP exchanges and uses URI templates to configure proxy locations. Configuration discovery and provisioning mechanisms are out of scope, allowing implementations flexibility.
sections.eli5: This is a test to see if this way of asking questions works well in the real world and is fast enough for people to use every day.
